messages.author: df5ef9058cfa4716
messages.subject: DSM segments
parts:
Hi, everybody!
I'll build a density surface model using line transect. I read that the segment length should be equal to twice the truncation distance, so as to have a segments areas approximately as squares. In my transects left and right are always different, different growth stages, so different visibility and detection function. This happens because I do the thermal along tracks that separate the different growth stages in the forest and it's not possible to do it in any other way in our study area. Is there a way to overcome this? 
Thank you

Valentina

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM segments
parts:
Valentina

Even if your truncation distances are different left and right of the transect, you can still set your segment length to roughly 2*(largest truncation distance).  The suggestion of transect length is just that, only a suggestion.  There are many decisions in your density surface analysis that are more important than segment length.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM segments
parts:
Hi Eric,

I have a question in addition to Valentina's regarding DSM segments and hence I thought it best to post here?

I am trying to decide the segment size for a DSM model where my parallel transects are 200 m apart and my maximum detection distance after 5% truncation is 75.6 m. I had 15 transects across a small study area, and transects were either 400, 800 or 1200 m long, hence I planned on dividing them into 200 m long segments to limit variability of animal density or covariate measurements within each segment, and to enable equal length segments. This will result in 66 x 200 m long segments. I am using remotely sensed data as part of the analysis and the resolution of this data is currently 50 x 50 m and 10 x 10 m. 

In this case, is it best that segment width is 2w and hence 151.2 m? Alternatively, should I increase the truncation and limit it to observations within 75 m and hence create a segment width of 150 m, which would neatly fit the resolution of the remotely sensed data, or would doing this be insignificant? 

Is it suitable to use a segment width beyond the truncation distance e.g. a 200 m wide segment? What are the consequences of creating segments greater than the truncation distance when creating a DSM? If I increased the segment width to 200 m, it would mean I effectively have complete coverage of the study area by the segments, is this an issue when performing DSM?

Any advice is much appreciated.

Regards,
Luke.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM segments
parts:
Luke

I would expect your results should be fairly insensitive to the different segment sizes you propose.  If you increase your segment width to 200m, resulting in complete coverage, there will be no model-based inference because there will not be any portion of your study area uncovered.

A paper dealing with segment size (on a considerably different scale than your study):

Redfern, J. V., Barlow, J., Ballance, L. T., Gerrodette, T., & Becker, E. A. (2008). Absence of scale dependence in dolphin–habitat models for the eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. Marine Ecology Progress Series, 363, 1–14. http://doi.org/10.3354/meps07495
